lead.tldr: Crypto startup fundraising Q2 strong: $76m raised, Pharos $44m Series A signals Layer-1 demand • Trump administration pushing Clarity Act, Senate review imminent, regulatory certainty could unlock US institutional capital • Morgan Stanley Bitcoin ETF draws $33m day‑one inflow, on track for $7bn AUM, indicating institutional appetite • Circle downgrade after Drift exploit raises stablecoin risk perception, USDC stability under heightened scrutiny • Bitcoin and Ethereum rally on low CPI and US‑Iran de‑escalation, but volatility may persist • Pyth Network data marketplace launches, offering monetized price feeds, could reduce oracle centralisation risk

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, this week we saw a $76 million fundraising surge, the push for the Clarity Act, and Morgan Stanley’s Bitcoin ETF on track for $7 bn. Meanwhile, stablecoin concerns and a heated layer‑2 debate added fresh dynamics to the market.

top_signals.title: Crypto startups kick off Q2 by raising $76m in the first week
top_signals.summary: Crypto startups raised a total of $76 million in the first week of Q2 2026, signaling a robust capital inflow at the start of the quarter despite ongoing geopolitical headwinds. The lead round was a $44 million Series A for Pharos, a high‑performance Layer‑1 blockchain platform, while AI‑focused Oh and payments‑oriented Kulipa secured the remaining funding. The fundraising activity highlights continued institutional appetite for infrastructure and application layers in the digital asset ecosystem. However, investors remain cautious, citing the US‑Iran conflict and broader macro‑economic uncertainty as factors that could temper future deployment of capital.

top_signals.title: Scott Bessent leads Trump administration push for Clarity Act as crucial deadline approaches
top_signals.summary: Scott Bessent is heading the Trump administration’s effort to move the Clarity Act through Congress. The Clarity Act is intended to give the U.S. crypto sector clear regulatory guidance, a factor that institutional investors view as essential for capital allocation decisions. With a Senate Banking Committee review scheduled for late April and a May deadline, officials and industry leaders are urging rapid passage to preserve market momentum.

top_signals.title: Morgan Stanley’s Bitcoin ETF on track to pull in $7bn in year one, says Ric Edelman
top_signals.summary: Morgan Stanley has launched a Bitcoin exchange‑traded fund that attracted $33 million in inflows on its first trading day. The firm projects the ETF will reach a $7 billion asset base within its first year. Financial adviser Ric Edelman says the fund is likely to draw capital from existing crypto ETFs, new client inflows, and expanding institutional acceptance. The product offers institutional investors a regulated avenue to gain exposure to Bitcoin while leveraging Morgan Stanley’s distribution network.

top_signals.title: Polymarket says it’s committed to US national security after another lawmaker slams betting platform
top_signals.summary: U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal sent a letter to the CEO of Polymarket alleging that the prediction‑market platform enables insider trading and allows wagers on events tied to national security. Polymarket responded that it has adopted new insider‑trading rules and reaffirmed its commitment to market integrity and U.S. national security. The exchange’s statements come as regulators maintain heightened scrutiny of the rapidly expanding crypto‑betting sector, which is of interest to institutional investors monitoring compliance and systemic risk.

top_signals.title: Circle Stock Falls Amid Downgrade as Drift Exploit Fallout Spreads
top_signals.summary: Circle, the issuer of the USDC stablecoin, saw its share price decline following a credit rating downgrade. The downgrade was linked to the ongoing fallout from the Drift exploit that affected USDC. Analysts cited heightened concerns about the stability and security of the broader stablecoin ecosystem as a key factor. The negative market reaction underscores the importance of robust risk management for institutional investors in digital‑asset exposures.

top_signals.title: ‘Cautious optimism’: Bitcoin, Ethereum shoot up following CPI release. How long will it last?
top_signals.summary: Bitcoin and Ethereum posted notable gains after U.S. consumer price index data indicated that core inflation increased by only 0.2% in March. The modest inflation reading has sparked cautious optimism among market participants that the Federal Reserve may consider a rate cut in the near term. The rally was further supported by a de‑escalation in tensions between the United States and Iran and by market speculation of a short squeeze, factors that institutional investors monitor for risk‑adjusted exposure decisions.

top_signals.title: Trump-backed WLFI token drops 12% to record lows after team defends multi-million lending position
top_signals.summary: The WLFI token issued by World Liberty Financial fell 12 percent to a record low after the company defended a multi‑million dollar lending position on the Dolomite DeFi platform. The firm disclosed that it had pledged its own governance token as collateral to borrow stablecoins, a practice that critics argue creates a circular risk loop. WLFI said it would increase token collateral to prevent liquidation of the loan. The episode has heightened concerns among investors about the protocol’s stability and the exposure of token holders to compounded risk.

top_signals.title: Ethereum is abandoning layer 2s. Arbitrum’s creator still sees a bright future ahead
top_signals.summary: Ethereum leadership is shifting focus to scaling the mainnet, which has prompted speculation about the future relevance of layer‑2 solutions such as Arbitrum. Offchain Labs co‑founder Ed Felten maintains that layer‑2 platforms continue to provide faster transaction processing and lower fees, keeping them pertinent to the network’s growth. The contrasting views illustrate a broader strategic debate within the Ethereum ecosystem that could influence investment decisions.

top_signals.title: Ripple's XRP may be less exposed to quantum computer threats than bitcoin
top_signals.summary: Ripple’s XRP is considered potentially less exposed to quantum computer threats than Bitcoin. Experts point to XRP’s built‑in key‑rotation and escrow time‑lock mechanisms that reduce vulnerability compared with Bitcoin’s practice of exposing public keys when transactions are broadcast. An audit of the XRP Ledger identified 300,000 accounts holding 2.4 billion XRP that have never sent funds, meaning their public keys remain hidden and quantum‑safe. This structural resilience may be relevant for institutional investors evaluating long‑term security of crypto holdings against emerging quantum‑computing risks.

top_signals.title: Pyth Network Launches Data Marketplace For Price Feeds Across Asset Classes
top_signals.summary: Pyth Network has introduced a data marketplace that aggregates price feeds covering a broad spectrum of asset classes. The marketplace enables data providers to list their feeds and earn revenue from them. Developers can access the aggregated price data directly on-chain, which is intended to improve the quality and reliability of price information used in decentralized applications. By offering a decentralized source of price data, the platform seeks to reduce the reliance on centralized data providers within the crypto ecosystem.

top_signals.title: Rapid Improvements in Foundation Models Surprise Even the Optimists
top_signals.summary: Anthropic introduced the Mythos foundation model, which marks a notable advance in automated software vulnerability detection. The company also announced Project Glasswing, a consortium that brings together Google, Microsoft, Amazon and other technology leaders to confront AI‑driven cybersecurity threats. Mythos’s ability to identify flaws without human intervention positions Anthropic as a frontier AI innovator and signals broader industry collaboration that could affect risk management strategies for institutional investors.

Startups raised $76 million, led by a $44 million Series A for Pharos, a high‑performance Layer‑1 platform. AI‑focused Oh and payments‑oriented Kulipa closed the round, showing that both core protocol work and real‑world use cases remain attractive to investors even as geopolitical tensions linger. At the same time, regulatory clarity is moving forward. Scott Bessent is steering the Trump administration’s push for the Clarity Act, a bill that promises to give the U.S. crypto sector a clear rulebook. With a Senate Banking Committee review slated for late April and a May deadline, industry leaders are urging swift passage to keep market momentum alive. On the institutional front, Morgan Stanley’s new Bitcoin ETF has already attracted $33 million on day one and is projected to reach a $7 billion asset base within its first year, according to Ric Edelman. The fund offers a regulated pathway for investors and leverages Morgan Stanley’s distribution power, hinting at a broader shift toward mainstream acceptance. At Blockwall we see these three threads, capital, clarity, and institutional products, converging to create a fertile environment for the next generation of crypto innovators.
